headline: High: Notion AI’s shared workspace access can feed Pipecat pipelines, creating default-path prompt-injection, leakage, and compliance risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Notion AI can read workspace pages and team knowledge base content, while Pipecat commonly ingests text through shared-bus conversation state and downstream LLM/STT/TTS services. If Notion content is routed into Pipecat without sanitization, attacker-controlled page text can steer prompts. The pairwise bridge is inferred, not directly documented, so uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF Notion page content is forwarded into Pipecat prompts or memory without filtering, injection is possible.
IF Pipecat treats upstream text as instructions rather than data, malicious workspace text can alter behavior.
mitigations: Add a prompt-delimiter and instruction/data separator in the Pipecat prompt template.
Strip or escape markup from Notion-sourced text before passing it onward.
Require a human review step for any Notion content that contains imperative language.
Disable automatic ingestion of arbitrary workspace pages into agent prompts.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags and instruction-blocking guards in the orchestration layer.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Notion AI touches workspace pages and team knowledge base content, and Pipecat handles text, conversation state, audio/video, and analytics over a shared bus. If the same workspace data is injected into Pipecat, sensitive content can flow into third-party model providers listed in Pipecat’s service surfaces. The leakage path is plausible in default integrations but not proven from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF workspace pages containing sensitive material are sent into Pipecat services, that material may leave the workspace boundary.
IF Pipecat is configured with external STT/LLM/TTS providers, copied Notion content can be transmitted onward.
mitigations: Limit Pipecat inputs to redacted excerpts only.
Turn off external provider routes for sensitive sessions.
Review and remove secrets from Notion pages before ingestion.
Set retention to the shortest available window in downstream services.
requires-engineering: enforce data-class allowlists between Notion and Pipecat.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Notion AI has no filesystem write, shell, or subprocess execution, while Pipecat exposes networked service integrations and shared-bus state. There is no direct overlapping write surface to the same local directory or git state in the profiles, so true capability conflict is limited. The main overlap is shared mutable conversation state, which is a smaller blast radius than filesystem contention.
conditions: IF both agents are wired to the same mutable conversation bus, state races can occur.
IF an operator maps Notion outputs into Pipecat memory without locking, overwrites are possible.
mitigations: Serialize writes to the shared bus.
Assign separate namespaces for each agent’s state.
Disable concurrent updates during critical turns.
Log last-writer metadata for each shared record.
requires-engineering: add optimistic locking to the orchestration layer.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Notion AI is a RAG-style Q&A system grounded in workspace content, and Pipecat can route text into LLM, memory, and action-oriented transports. If Pipecat treats Notion output as authoritative, errors or hallucinations can cascade into downstream actions. The profiles support the pathway, but there is no direct evidence of an action-taking workflow, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF Pipecat consumes Notion answers without verification, incorrect facts can propagate.
IF downstream Pipecat flows trigger external actions, a mistaken Notion answer can cause real-world side effects.
mitigations: Insert a verification step before any downstream action.
Require citations or source links from Notion outputs.
Block action execution when confidence is low or missing.
Use a second model to cross-check critical claims.
requires-engineering: add policy gates before any external side effect.

E_compliance.rationale: Notion AI processes workspace pages and team knowledge base content under the invoking user’s Notion permissions, while Pipecat can send text, audio, and analytics to multiple external providers. If regulated or residency-bound data from Notion enters Pipecat’s allowlisted third-party services, retention and jurisdiction mismatches can arise. The profiles do not prove a specific regime, so this remains medium rather than high.
conditions: IF EU PII or regulated content from Notion is routed to non-contracted Pipecat providers, residency/compliance issues arise.
IF downstream services retain transcripts longer than the workspace policy, retention mismatch occurs.
mitigations: Restrict the pair to non-regulated content only.
Choose providers with matching residency and DPA terms.
Disable analytics export for sensitive sessions.
Document retention settings for each downstream service.
requires-engineering: implement compliance routing by data class and region.
